# Jubilees Chapter 34 — The EMET Bible (Literal)
**Translator:** EMET | **Source:** Ge'ez MS; cf. 4QJub (Hebrew fragments) | **Section:** The war of Jacob against the Amorite kings; Joseph taken by Midianites

---

**34:1** In the sixth year of the third week of the forty-fifth jubilee, Jacob and all his sons went and dwelt in the land of the east at Shechem.

**34:2** And the seven Amorite kings gathered themselves together against Jacob and his sons to slay them, drawing out their swords. And Jacob's sons prevailed over them and slew them in the highlands of Shechem. And they seized all their herds and all their possessions.

**34:3** And Judah slew Mahalath, and Dan slew his king, and Naphtali slew Hazor, and Gad slew Phineas, and Asher slew Boaz the king of Betoron, and Zebulun slew his king, and Reuben slew his king.

**34:4** And they slew these seven kings and carried off all their possessions and became great. And they enclosed the spoil in the city of Shechem.

**34:5** And in the seventh year of this week, Joseph went to Dothan to seek his brothers, and he did not find them in Dothan but went east to Shechem. And he found them there.

**34:6** And his brothers saw him and plotted against him to slay him. And Judah said: "Let us sell him to the Ishmaelites who are passing." And they agreed to it.

**34:7** And the Midianite merchants passed by and drew Joseph out of the pit, and sold him to the Ishmaelites for twenty pieces of silver. And they brought him to Egypt.

**34:8** And his brothers killed a kid of the goats and dipped Joseph's coat in the blood and sent it to their father Jacob.

**34:9** And Jacob mourned Joseph greatly and said: "An evil beast hath devoured him." And Jacob rent his garments, and put on sackcloth, and mourned for Joseph many days.

**34:10** And Rebekah's maidservant Deborah died, and Jacob buried her under the oak by Bethel, and called the name of the place The Oak of Weeping.

**34:11** And in the forty-fifth jubilee, in the fifth week, in the first year, Jacob sent Judah to his father Isaac, and Isaac strengthened him, and Jacob had joy before his father Isaac, and Jacob's sons loved Isaac greatly.

**34:12** And when Isaac was sick, his two sons Esau and Jacob came to him, and he was comforted, and said: "The days of my years are complete, being a hundred and eighty years old."

**34:13** And in the sixth week, in the first year, in the forty-fifth jubilee, Isaac died, being exceedingly old. And his two sons Esau and Jacob buried him.

**34:14** And Esau went to the land of Edom to the mountains of Seir, and left his sons there. And Jacob remained at Mamre opposite Hebron.

**34:15** And the sons of Jacob went each man to his wife and begat sons and daughters. And they were twelve altogether including Benjamin.

**34:16** And the sons of Reuben were Enoch and Phallu and Hezron and Carmi — four. And the sons of Simeon were Jemuel and Jamin and Ohad and Jachin and Zohar — five. And the sons of Levi were Gershon and Kohath and Merari — three. And the sons of Judah were Er and Onan and Shelah and Perez and Zerah — five.

**34:17** And in that time, in the second year of the sixth week, there was a famine in all the land, except in Egypt. And Jacob sent his sons except Benjamin to buy grain from Egypt.

**34:18** And Joseph had become ruler over all Egypt, and he was the master of all the storehouses of Pharaoh, and he was thirty years old when he came before Pharaoh.

**34:19** And when the sons of Jacob came to Egypt, Joseph recognized them but they did not recognize him.

**34:20** And Joseph commanded and said to them: "Bring your younger brother to me." And he kept Simeon with him until they returned with Benjamin his brother.

---

*EMET notes: Chapter 34 contains material not in Genesis: the war of Jacob against the seven Amorite kings (vv.1-4) is unique to Jubilees and the Testament of Judah. The Joseph narrative (vv.5-20) compresses Genesis 37 significantly. The genealogies of the twelve sons are partially listed.*
